name: numbeo-sql-importer
what_it_holds: Official Numbeo org repo ('Numbeo API Example – Retrieve Cost of Living for a City'); importer that loads Numbeo API responses into SQL. No bulk dataset committed — requires a paid Numbeo API key to pull data.
why_useful: This is the official/authorized path into Numbeo's data (via their paid API, not scraping), which sidesteps the ToS concern the repo rules flag for direct scraping of crowdsourced travel sites — worth flagging to a human as the 'ask for budget' option instead of an ad hoc scraper.
themes: Currency and travel affordability crowdsourced data: Numbeo, Expatistan, hotel price indices (Hotels.com HPI archives), Trivago Hotel Price Index, Kayak price trackers
why_all: This is the official/authorized path into Numbeo's data (via their paid API, not scraping), which sidesteps the ToS concern the repo rules flag for direct scraping of crowdsourced travel sites — worth flagging to a human as the 'ask for budget' option instead of an ad hoc scraper.
Confirms Numbeo has an official (paid) API path with structured city cost-of-living data; relevant if the team ever licenses Numbeo data directly rather than scraping.

name: GarysCorner/NewORleansSTR
what_it_holds: Jupyter notebook (STRMaps.ipynb) that pulls New Orleans's 'Short-Term Rental Licenses' dataset from the city's open-data portal (data.nola.gov) and renders it as an interactive folium/Leaflet map of active STR license status. No historical snapshots committed — reads the live current portal export. 3 stars, updated 5 Aug 2026 (active).
why_useful: New Orleans is not in our current municipal-registry list (Austin, Barcelona, Maui, NYC, California TOT cities); this notebook is a working, recently-updated method for pulling that city's STR license registry directly from its Socrata-style open-data portal — cheap to adapt into our own point-in-time puller.
size_hint: notebook + generated HTML map, no bulk data file
duplicate_of_holding: Municipal STR registries panel (Austin/Barcelona/Maui/NYC/California) — adds a new city, not a duplicate
themes: University and municipal research datasets on STRs published on GitHub (city planning departments, urban labs, McGill UPGo, Inside Airbnb collaborators)

name: UPGo-McGill/vancouver-regulations
what_it_holds: Analysis of STR host compliance with Vancouver's 2018 STR licensing regulations. Committed data/raffle.csv (~7.7 MB) — appears to be the output of the raffle geocoding method applied to Vancouver STR listings, i.e. a listing-level (or listing-day-level) dataset with assigned neighbourhood/geography and likely licence-compliance flags.
why_useful: Directly on-point for gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration trackers) for Vancouver, one of the cities named in that gap list.
themes: University and municipal research datasets on STRs published on GitHub (city planning departments, urban labs, McGill UPGo, Inside Airbnb collaborators)

name: fbi
what_it_holds: A client library for the FBI's Crime Data Explorer API, exposing UCR (Uniform Crime Reporting) and NIBRS (National Incident-Based Reporting System) crime data by agency/city/state. Last updated 2024-03-11.
why_useful: A one-command pull method for US city-level crime statistics, which is one of this theme's three named data types (crime by city). Crime trends by city could be tested as a local demand-shock proxy for STR bookings in specific US metros (Austin, New Orleans, Chicago -- all in our 13-city panel).
time_coverage: pulls whatever history the FBI Crime Data Explorer API exposes (UCR historically back to 1960 at state level, NIBRS more recent and more granular by agency)
size_hint: small client library, no committed data
themes: Insurance, safety and travel advisories datasets (State Dept advisories history, travel insurance claims, crime by city) as demand shocks
why_all: A one-command pull method for US city-level crime statistics, which is one of this theme's three named data types (crime by city). name: fbi-crime-mcp-server
what_it_holds: An MCP server wrapping the FBI Crime Data Explorer API -- UCR crime estimates, NIBRS incident breakdowns, hate crimes, arrests, human trafficking stats. 1 star, updated 2026-08-21 (actively maintained, most recent of the FBI-API clients found).
why_useful: Same underlying source as the Pirshtuk/fbi client (US city/agency-level crime data) but more recently maintained and packaged as an MCP tool, which could be plugged directly into an agent pipeline for pulling city crime series without writing scraper code.
